What is the deeper meaning of the forest simile of the deep anchor in a mountain lake used in 'For the Love of the World' (Ānāpānasati The Discourse on Mindfulness of Breathing abbreviated and adapted) concerning 'In this way you are cultivating'?

In this section of *For the Love of the World*, the Dhamma is brought to life: *"In this way you are cultivating the enlightenment factor of mindfulness; which, thus developed, reaches fulfillment."*. The Forest Tradition relies on direct nature imagery because the mind operates through experiential resonance rather than abstract logic. It is like a small boat moored to a deep anchor on a vast mountain lake: waves may roll on the surface, but the anchor keeps the boat steady. When you hold this simile in your heart during practice, it provides an immediate reference point for letting go and realizing unburdened clarity.
